applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public MYP page describes the programme as for students aged 11-16 and as a five-year programme that schools may shorten. Mapping Grade 6 (often about ages 11-12) onto the start of that span is our convention, not an IB grade or MYP-year boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Florida Grade 6 science is the 2016 NGSSS grade list, not a new B.E.S.T. science course. MYP does not replace that adoption. Do not read integrated-science eAssessment as a Grade 6 requirement.

subject_group_or_structure.mapping_to_primer_subject: Grade 6 Florida NGSSS science (SC.6) is mapped here to the MYP sciences subject group. The public page says courses usually include biology, chemistry, and physics, and that schools may offer other courses, including earth sciences and life sciences. It does not publish a Grade 6 syllabus.

official_requirements.text: The International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) is for students aged 11-16.

official_requirements.text: The MYP is a five-year programme, which can be implemented in a partnership between schools, or in several abbreviated (two, three or four year) formats.

official_requirements.text: Using global contexts, MYP students develop an understanding of their common humanity and shared guardianship of the planet through developmentally appropriate explorations of: identities and relationships; personal and cultural expression; orientations in space and time; scientific and technical innovation; fairness and development; globalization and sustainability.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The sciences subject brief names four equally weighted assessment criteria: A Knowing and understanding; B Inquiring and designing; C Processing and evaluating; D Reflecting on the impacts of science. The 1-8 band descriptors are not stored here.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 6 Florida science in this draft covers scientific investigation, energy, motion, forces, cells and human body systems, classification, the nature of scientific knowledge, and Earth structures, weather, and climate. Those benchmarks are NGSSS. A reasonable MYP fit is inquiry, design, and processing data (criteria B and C), plus knowing scientific ideas (criterion A), without treating the Florida big-idea list as an IB syllabus. Earth and life topics can sit in courses the sciences page allows schools to offer. That is not a claim that MYP requires the Florida Grade 6 list.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Defining a problem and carrying out an investigation fits criterion B Inquiring and designing. The “sixth grade curriculum” phrase is Florida’s.
Explaining why investigations should be replicable fits processing and evaluating. MYP does not print that sentence as an objective.
Distinguishing a scientific theory from everyday use of the word theory fits knowing and understanding. The Florida wording is not an IB criterion descriptor.
The Law of Gravity as every object attracting every other object is a Florida benchmark. The public MYP pages do not state that law.
Cell theory can sit under knowing scientific ideas. The three cell-theory claims are Florida’s.
Interactions among Earth spheres can connect to the example key concept of systems. Naming geosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere is Florida’s.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
